svg.title: Automated inlay line versus manual bench throughput, and the arithmetic that exposes an inflated capacity claim
svg.desc: An automated line (Mühlbauer TAL-15000, Ruhlamat ProLine, Melzer flip-chip) runs 6,000 to 30,000 units per hour. A manual bench runs 200 to 800 units per hour. A factory claiming 5 million units per month on three manual benches: three benches times 800 units per hour, running flat out 24 by 7, equals 1,728,000 per month. The remaining 3,272,000 is coming from a factory you have not audited.
svg.text: DO THE ARITHMETIC, WATCH THE STORY FALL OVER
Mühlbauer TAL-15000 · Ruhlamat ProLine · Melzer flip-chip
three benches and, you'll recall, one very patient operator
(bars not to scale — that's rather the point)
THE CLAIM: 5,000,000 UNITS / MONTH — ON THREE MANUAL BENCHES
…and that's flat out, no breaks, no sleep, no Chinese New Year.
The other 3,272,000 is coming from a factory you haven't audited.
A converter claiming volume it can't physically produce is subcontracting — quietly, and to a floor you never get to inspect.
